about.title: Aliso Viejo Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Aliso Viejo's mix of shopping centers, office parks, and residential complexes near Aliso Creek Road and Pacific Park Drive means plenty of walkways, stairwells, and parking areas where a spill, cracked pavement, or poor lighting can cause a serious fall. Under California law, a property owner or manager generally has to have known, or reasonably should have known, about a hazardous condition and failed to fix or warn about it before they can be held responsible. That's why documenting the scene matters so much: photos of the hazard, witness names, and a request to preserve any surveillance footage before it's overwritten can make a real difference. We handle premises liability cases for people hurt in falls around Aliso Viejo and can evaluate the notice issue, the property's maintenance history, and what your claim may be worth. There's no cost for a free case review, and no fee unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Notice and Evidence

items.title: Notice Is the Core Issue
items.desc: California premises liability claims turn on whether the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. We can help gather maintenance logs, complaint history, and inspection records to establish that.

items.title: Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Surveillance footage from stores and complexes near Aliso Viejo Parkway or Alicia Parkway is often overwritten within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation can protect evidence that supports your claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, a Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for the fall, you may still recover a reduced amount. We can help present the facts fairly.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Aliso Viejo?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a government or public entity, that deadline is much shorter and involves a separate claims process, so it's worth checking quickly.

items.question: What if I fell at a shopping center near Aliso Viejo Town Center?
items.answer: Commercial properties in busy corridors like Pacific Park Drive often have multiple parties involved, such as the landlord, a tenant store, or a maintenance contractor. We can help sort out who's responsible before evidence like video or spill logs disappears.

items.question: Will I still have a case if I was partly at fault for not seeing the hazard?
items.answer: Possibly, yes. California follows pure comparative fault, meaning your recovery could be reduced by your percentage of responsibility but isn't automatically barred. We can review the specifics of what happened.
